title: San Francisco with Oliver and the dispute that ended it
summary: The band went to San Francisco with Davey Jones added; Hall refused to lay off Jimmy Palao, Oliver dismissed him, the union ruled in his favour, and he returned to Chicago to work with Jimmy Noone.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So some man up there, I forget his name, he wanted a Dixland band to work at a place called Pekrola Dance Hall on Market Street. I have a picture of that. Yeah, so he got in touch with these guys, so we had to add another man to the band to make eight pieces. So he picked up a fellow by the name of Jones. Well, Davey Jones.

He's still here. He's a historian. Yeah, he lives here. He was playing saxophone there. So after he joined the band, and Oliver was taking his job to San Francisco, that's when we went to San Francisco and work up there. So after we started working there a while, I don't know, maybe the people didn't go for Dixland, so they would go to the dance hall like they did. So Oliver wanted to lay off one man. So we think he should lay off Jones instead of Jimmy Pala. So that's when the mix-up come up. So I told him, I said, well, I'll have to stick with Jim. I said, we'll all come up together, and I don't see why I should lay him off. So Oliver got kind of peeved about it. So he says, well, if you don't like it, you can go with him just like that. Well, he tried to say that I quit, but I didn't. So in the meantime, he gave me a notice, and so the union taken it up. So we had a case, and we had to go for the board about it. So when I wound up, they made him pay me all my expenses back home, and I think it made him pay me a month's work or something like that. And they found him around $150 for sending for Baby Dots. That's how Baby Dots got to play with him. See, he sent for Baby Dots without getting permission from the union. And if I'm not mistaken, I think they found him $300. So that's how I fell out with Oliver. So at the meantime, I went back to Chicago. And when I went back to Chicago, Jimmy Noon hired me. So at the meantime, Tegra was playing with Carl Dixon, the big band at Sunset across the street from where I was working. The place we were working at, I opened up with Jimmy Noon, Earl Hines, Joe Poston, and if I'm not mistaken, I think Johnny was playing, I'm not sure. Was that the drums? No, see. The drummer, I was trying to think. No, no, no. I mean you went in the 40th. We opened the place. You opened the whole.
At that time they called it the Ness.
